What is Roblox? ROBLOX is an online virtual playground and workshop, where kids of all ages can safely interact, create, have fun, and learn. It’s unique in that practically everything on ROBLOX is designed and constructed by members of the community.  Each player starts by choosing an avatar and giving it an identity. They can then explore ROBLOX — interacting with others by chatting, playing games, or collaborating on creative projects. Each player is also given their own piece of undeveloped real estate along with a virtual toolbox with which to design and build anything — be it a navigable skyscraper, a working helicopter, a giant pinball machine, a multiplayer “Capture the Flag” game or some other, yet-to-be-dreamed-up creation. There is no cost for this first plot of virtual land. By participating and by building cool stuff, ROBLOX members can earn specialty badges as well as ROBLOX dollars (“Robux”). In turn, they can shop the online catalog to purchase avatar clothing and accessories as well as premium building materials, interactive components, and working mechanisms.

snippet.title: RESIDENT EVIL – Official Trailer (4K)
snippet.description:
𝙽𝚘 𝚜𝚠𝚎𝚊𝚝.
 
From the mind of Zach Cregger, director of Weapons and Barbarian. Watch the official trailer for Resident Evil. Filmed for IMAX – in theatres 9.18. #ResidentEvil

https://www.instagram.com/residentevil/
https://twitter.com/ResidentEvil
https://www.facebook.com/ResidentEvilMovie
https://www.tiktok.com/@resident.evil.movie

From the mind of visionary filmmaker Zach Cregger (Weapons, Barbarian) comes a thrilling — and terrifying — reinvention of the Resident Evil franchise. In an all-new story, Resident Evil follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who unwittingly finds himself in an action-packed, non-stop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos.
 
From Columbia Pictures and Constantin Film, in association with TriStar Pictures, Resident Evil hits theatres September 18, 2026.

Directed by: Zach Cregger   
 
Written by: Zach Cregger & Shay Hatten    

Produced by:
Robert Kulzer
Zach Cregger
Roy Lee

Carter Swan
Asad Qizilbash

Executive Producers:
Oliver Berben

Robert Bernacci

Cast:

snippet.title: Build Detectives: Episode 0
snippet.description:

snippet.title: ORC INCREMENTAL Is A Perfectly Balanced Game With No E̲X̲P̲L̲O̲I̲T̲S̲
snippet.description:
Welcome to a brand new perfectly balanced video game from the publisher of Cookie Clicker. This is Orc Incremental The incremental auto battler. Where you build an orc army, watch it fight, and make it unstoppable! Now I am the spiffing brit breaker of video games as I love to find overpowered bugs, glitches and exploits inside of them to do silly things and this game is no different! It might be a demo for  an unreleased game but that will not stop me!

So what is Orc Incremental well it is rather simple you start with a single orc and build an unstoppable dark army to conquer the realms in this incremental auto battler. Perfect your formation, summon mighty beasts, unlock powerful upgrades, and grow stronger with each rebirth. Think of it like cookie clicker but we make money by defeating armies of good and happy elves working with knights and peasants. 
This is NOT sponsored but you can checkout the game on steam here and give it a Wishlist if you like: https://store.steampowered.com/app/4047270/Orc_Incremental/

snippet.title: "Silicon Valley" - Marsh Family arrangement of traditional American folk song "Down in the Valley"
snippet.description:
‘Down in the Valley’ – sometimes also known as ‘Birmingham Jail’ – is a traditional American folk song that was circulating in earnest in the 1920s. Versions have been recorded by a huge set of music icons, with our favourites including those of Pete Seeger, Tex Ritter, the Blue Ridge Mountain Boys, Solomon Burke, and a Glen Campbell version which encouraged us to include modulations up a perfect fourth cos they’re very uplifting. 

The song comes from a deep heritage mixing English, Irish, Scottish, Appalachian, and Ozark influences, with its distinctive mournful (perhaps jailhouse) waltz. For our version we’ve stepped away from a love ballad, but there is a lament in the arrangement and it hopefully feels resonant of US pioneer history. It contemplates how some of the more progressive ideas that were kindled by early generations of Silicon Valley entrepreneurs have been flamboyantly cast aside by the latest cohort, as they move aggressively to embrace a different set of values – scrabbling for an ever-more concentrated and destructive matrix of resources and power, while backfilling flimsy self-oriented rationales. Not that US tech or Silicon Valley didn’t always have its fair share of corporate greed, competition, and self-promotion, but there was often at least a veneer of social conscience, environmental mindfulness, techno-altruism, and a kind of confidence and coolness that the current crop of tech bros have lost, as they suck at whatever teat will fit with their fantasies of deregulation, accumulation, and self-glorification. 

For info on the folk song: https://balladofamerica.org/down-in-the-valley/

For info on the history of Silicon Valley: Margaret O’Mara, The Code: Silicon Valley and the Remaking of America (2019); on the biography of William Shockley: Joel Shurkin, Broken Genius (2006)

To buy this song as a download on Bandcamp: https://themarshfamily.bandcamp.com/track/silicon-valley

___________________________

DIGITAL: https://orcd.co/hollowchapters 
PHYSICAL: CDs or LPs: https://themarshfamily.bandcamp.com/album/hollow-chapters

- https://open.spotify.com/artist/6AYmbCwi92V29y69lkRkRa 

___________________________ 

LYRICS

Silicon Valley, where did you go? 
Used to be kind of get-up-and-go
That chapter’s over – new colours show
Something’s come over every tech bro

Pioneer spirits, once broke new ground
Frontier outfits, set to astound
New moral compass turned them around
Now like the Donners, they’ll eat what they’ve found

They treat the world like Lord of the Rings
They riddle Earth with crypto-mined kings
Buying up puppets, pulling the strings
Be a good hobbit: don’t clip their wings

Paranoid hubris, clinging like smoke
Crass manifestos clichés invoke
Stuck in denial, whingin’ ‘bout ‘woke’
Endlessly wealthy, somehow they’re broke

Silicon Valley, let us regale
William Shockley’s cautionary tale
Legendary founder, went off the rail
From a success to cultural fail

From Palo Alto, hungry and smart
He hit the East Coast, got a kick-start
Helped out in wartime, playing his part
Prize-winning research: state of the art

Solid-state physics, brain full of sparks
Semi-conductors, making his mark
Signed up to Stanford, start-ups embarked
But Shockley’s journey turned pretty dark

Habits got grumpy, sacked employees
Troublesome mindset, quite hard to please
Spouted eugenics, false expertise
Funded by fascists, causing unease

Kind of psychotic, behind the scenes
Gave to a sperm bank, proud of his genes
Went from a legend, making machines
To a sad end, like his little beans

What will your new breed leave us behind?
Fixing the climate, great new designs?
Rocketing wealth gaps, unchecked AI
Shitgibbon history, Bond villain minds

Silicon Valley, what of you’s left?
Every back-alley seems to be cleft
Hitched to your new mule, journey’s bereft
Where will it lead to: damage and theft

snippet.title: Firearms Expert Reacts to Max Payne 1 & 2 Guns | EXP
snippet.description:
EXP is the premium destination for your favourite expert-driven content, all funded by the fans. Get early access and extended episodes every week at: https://Patreon.com/WatchEXP

Check out our brand new Cursed Merch! Go to https://expvideo.info to see our new range, which includes T-Shirts, Hoodies, Pint Glasses, Posters, Stickers, and a very fetching Hawaiian-themed shirt! 

Jonathan Ferguson, an expert in firearms history, and the Keeper of Firearms & Artillery at the Royal Armouries Museum in the UK, reacts to the the weapons of Max Payne 1 & 2, including Max's iconic Beretta (complete with grimace), a highly detailed Colt Commando (for 2001 at least), and the shotgun to end all shotguns: the Pancor Jackhammer (sadly without landmine capability).

00:00 - Intro
01:33 - Beretta (Max Payne) 
06:44 - Beretta 9mm (Max Payne 2)
11:17 - Pump-Action Shotgun (Max Payne)
12:59 - Pump-Action Shotgun (Max Payne 2)
14:39 - Desert Eagle (Max Payne)
16:10 - Desert Eagle (Max Payne 2)
16:45 - Ingram (Max Payne)
18:11 - Ingram (Max Payne 2)
18:42 - MP5 (Max Payne)
20:51 - Sniper Rifle (Max Payne)
22:23 - Sniper Rifle (Max Payne 2)
23:58 - Dragunov (Max Payne 2)
25:31 - Colt Commando (Max Payne)
27:17 - M4 Carbine (Max Payne 2)
29:13 - Kalashnikov (Max Payne 2)
30:59 - Jackhammer (Max Payne)
32:18 - Striker (Max Payne 2)

In this episode of Expert Reacts on EXP, Jonathan Ferguson--an expert in firearms history and the Keeper of Firearms & Artillery at the Royal Armouries Museum in the UK--breaks down guns of Max Payne 1 & 2, and compares them to their real-life counterparts with artefacts from the Royal Armouries archive.

If you're interested in seeing more of Jonathan's work, you can check out more from the Royal Armouries right here. - https://www.youtube.com/user/RoyalArmouries  

If you would like to support the Royal Armouries, you can make a charitable donation to the museum here. - https://royalarmouries.org/support-us/donate

And if you would like to become a member of the Royal Armouries, you can get a membership here. - https://royalarmouries.org/support-us/become-a-member

You can purchase Jonathan's book here. - https://www.headstamppublishing.com/bullpup-rifle-book

You can subscribe to the Armax Journal that Jonathan Associate Edited here: https://www.armaxjournal.org/

snippet.title: Minecraft punishes casual players. I made a datapack to fix it.
snippet.description:
You can find the datapack here: https://modrinth.com/datapack/matcha-flavoured 

Special thank you to Ciren, for composing the “Golden” Music Disc. Seriously, Ciren, you’re amazing.

If you think YOU can make a killer music disc *or* would like to donate a track to the pack, email me!
If you think YOU can make better textures and would like to donate some for the pack, email me!


Mods I recommend using with the pack:
    Easy Shulker Boxes
       https://modrinth.com/mod/easy-shulker-boxes  
    Bundle Upgrade
       https://modrinth.com/mod/bundle-upgrade 
    Ambient Sounds
       https://modrinth.com/mod/ambientsounds 
    Cosy Critters & Creepy Crawlies
       https://modrinth.com/mod/cosy-critters  
    Particle Rain
       https://modrinth.com/mod/particle-rain 
    Better Clouds
       https://modrinth.com/mod/better-clouds 

    These mods can be easily added and removed and I’ve had no issue loading a new version without
    them. In other words, they seem to be ever-green, and when the authors stop updating them, you 
    don't have to worry about the mods corrupting your world upon removal. 

Inspirational Artists & Works*¹*
    Raspberry Flavoured - Raspmary
       Go check out Raspmary’s modpack here: https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/modpacks/raspberry-flavoured 
       I really enjoyed my time with Raspberry Flavoured. I think the design and attention to the resource 
       economy and progression was stellar. Truly reworking the create mod into a brilliantly designed 
       progression. I can’t give this modpack more praise.
       Electrum, Shakudo, Hepatizon, and Divine Fragments were directly inspired by this mod; plus 
       much more!
    JermsyBoy
       My resource pack was made to mirror JermsyBoy’s original texture pack as closely as possible. I 
       thought he did great work but unfortunately has since stopped developing the project. Further, the 
       textures had copyright protections on them, thus my pack was made to mimic it whilst still allowing 
       everyone to modify and steal textures as they wish.
       His original texture pack: https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/texture-packs/a-little-taste-of-jerm 
       He also has a youtube channel, and has some stunning builds: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCICnSwa3x5sHTWmTP6YO30w 
    MiziraGamez
       Provided a framework for endless repairing (No XP cap)
       You can find their datapack here: https://modrinth.com/datapack/repair-cost-remover 
    Gooporeal
       Provided inspiration for the Lichen re-models I did
       Their resource pack: https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/gooporeals-lichen 
    Vectorwing
       Provided the inspiration for a lot of my textures 
       Their resourcepack: https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/texture-packs/detail-brush 
       (Gorgeous work)
    Rhythmic under PurpurMC
       Provided a framework for looting shears. 
       Their datapack: https://modrinth.com/datapack/purpurpacks-looting-shears?version=26.1&loader=datapack 
    Matt Colville
       https://www.youtube.com/@mcolville 
       I realise Mr. Colville’s inspirations may not be obvious. Mr. Colville informed a lot of my design 
       philosophy. He, I think, introduced me to the idea that overpowered is a bad question, that we should
       instead think about how much fun something is. I'm sure there's countless other things he informed, he 
       he certainly is a big reason I choose to still make art in spite of the challenges.

    [1] *These people do not know me nor endorse me.* I have been *inspired* by them. If you like this 
            video, you may also enjoy the work these people do.

Media References & Attributions (In order of appearance)
    Draper, H. (1898) The Lament for Icarus
    Breath of the Wild (2017) Nintendo.
    Dark Souls: Remastered (2018) FromSoftware. Namco Bandai Games
    Stemonitis (2010) Cutter Mattock. Wikimedia
    Grote, K. (2006) Hedemue Pionieraexte. Wikimedia


 Music Attributions
    Raine, L. (2022) Firebugs. Minecraft: The Wild Update
    fingerspit (2026) Shores. Minecraft: Chaos Cubed
    C418 (2013) Dreiton. Minecraft - Volume Beta
    C418 (2011) Chris. Minecraft - Volume Alpha
    C418 (2013) Haunt Muskie. Minecraft - Volume Beta
    fingerspit (2026) III - The Gardener. The Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood OST
    River Boy (2022) Temple. Cult of the Lamb OST.
    River Boy (2022) Faith Up. Cult of the Lamb OST.
    C418 (2013) Ki. Minecraft - Volume Beta
